name: Fairfield Greenwich

summary.text: Fairfield Greenwich Group ran the Fairfield Sentry funds, the largest 'feeder' funds into Bernard Madoff's investment business; Massachusetts regulators said more than 95 percent of the Sentry funds' $7.2 billion in assets was placed with Madoff. In 2009 the firm settled a Massachusetts Securities Division action for $8 million without admitting or denying the allegations. In 2011 the Madoff bankruptcy trustee settled with the liquidators of Fairfield Sentry, Sigma and Lambda, reducing Sentry's claim from $1.2 billion to $230 million and recovering $70 million, and in 2012 the firm agreed to a settlement with investors worth up to about $80.3 million.

facts.claim: Massachusetts Secretary of State William Galvin's office said Fairfield Greenwich placed more than 95 percent of its Sentry funds' $7.2 billion in assets with Madoff's firm; the firm responded that it had made clear to investors that Madoff held substantially all of the Sentry funds' assets.

facts.claim: In 2009 Fairfield Greenwich Group settled the Massachusetts Securities Division's action for $8 million under a consent order entered without admitting or denying the allegations, which concerned three Sentry funds sold to Massachusetts investors; it was described as the first such agreement with a state regulator.

sources.title: MA Gets $8M Settlement over Madoff Investments
Mass. Won't Settle for Madoff 'Feeder' Offer

facts.claim: In May 2011 the Madoff trustee Irving Picard reached a settlement with the liquidators of Fairfield Sentry, Fairfield Sigma and Fairfield Lambda under which Sentry's customer claim was reduced from $1.2 billion to $230 million, the liquidators paid $70 million to the customer fund, and the trustee dropped pursuit of $3.8 billion from the liquidators.

facts.claim: A bankruptcy judge approved a $212 million settlement between the trustee and two bankrupt Greenwich Sentry funds; investors in Fairfield Sentry objected and the trustee agreed they could pursue the fund managers to recoup losses.

facts.claim: In November 2012 Bloomberg reported that Fairfield Greenwich agreed to a settlement with investors that could pay as much as $80.3 million.
